quotes.text: All payment methods are initially disabled by default.
A customer sees only payment methods that are turned on and compatible with the payment location and currency.
Checkout supports Apple Pay and Google Pay with no integration changes.
You can’t exclude Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Link on a per-transaction basis using `excluded_payment_method_types`.

old_evidence.text: By default, Apple Pay is enabled and Google Pay is disabled.

findings: Both old raw lines 8-23 and new raw lines 9-24 require dynamic payment methods with Payment Element or Checkout. The merchant/connected-account platform can create named configuration sets for product groups, one-time versus subscription scenarios, or a connected-account offering. Checkout chooses a configuration, and Stripe filters the methods by eligibility and currency/location restrictions and ranks enabled methods to optimize conversion, not guaranteed display.

Old raw lines 25-82 and new raw lines 26-70 retain the Default Config plus Dashboard and API creation. A new Dashboard configuration initially has methods disabled; the merchant separately activates the configuration and toggles methods. API examples may set per-method `display_preference.preference` to `on`, and `name` is the Dashboard-readable label. The default common Checkout payment methods discussion is separate from new configuration state.

Old raw lines 84-144 and 156-175 and new raw lines 72-124 and 134-147 preserve selecting the ID: Web deferred Payment Element uses `paymentMethodConfiguration`; iOS/Android deferred PaymentSheet intent configuration samples use `paymentMethodConfigurationId`; Checkout Session without Payment Element or server PaymentIntent creation uses `payment_method_configuration`. `automatic_payment_methods` is described as optional in the capture's latest API, with examples explicitly setting it. Current source lines 18 and 21 can imply every Payment Element flow accepts the ID; scope these client-side samples to deferred intent creation and keep the active/configuration-versus-payment states distinct.

Both captures distinguish broad reusable configurations from narrow per-transaction exclusions and allow using them together. Excluding Apple Pay, Google Pay or Link uses integration-specific `wallets` parameters (old raw lines 177-194 and new raw lines 149-166). The separate November API configuration endpoint overview at raw/stripe-api-payment-method-configurations-2026-11-07.md lines 25-33 distinguishes own-account direct configurations from connected-account child configurations and Dashboard-managed parents. That is separate authority, not a new behavior of this guide.

Both guides require dynamic payment methods (old raw lines 20-23, new raw lines 21-24). Their server examples select the configuration ID without explicitly listing payment method types (old raw lines 125-144 and 156-175; new raw lines 113-124 and 134-147). The 2026-11-07 Payment Method Configurations API overview line 25 explicitly limits this selection to when payment method types are not explicitly specified. The merchant or platform selects the configuration ID and Stripe filters and ranks its eligible enabled methods.

Current source line 20 displays `pm` as if it were a literal top-level creation field. The old raw lines 55-73 and new raw lines 56-62 show actual named method keys `affirm` and `klarna`, each with `display_preference.preference` set to `on`. Use a real method name or label `pm` as a placeholder, and retain separate Dashboard activation and initial method-disabled state.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 full guide at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-method-configurations documents merchants using dynamic payment methods with Payment Element or Checkout. New raw lines 9-70 and 72-166 describe creating or selecting a named configuration, Dashboard activation and per-method enablement. The merchant or platform selects the configuration ID when using dynamic selection without an explicit payment method types list, as the same-date configuration API overview specifies. Stripe filters enabled methods by eligible currency and location and ranks them. The create examples use named fields such as affirm and klarna rather than a literal pm field. Deferred Web and native client setup uses platform-specific configuration fields. A Checkout Session or server-created PaymentIntent takes the REST field. A configuration and per-transaction exclusions can be combined, with separate wallet visibility controls. Old raw lines 8-194 establish the same core flow, but state specific Checkout wallet defaults and tax/shipping behavior. source-stripe-payment-method-configurations.md summarizes the flow but needs dated wallet wording and explicit activation and deferred-platform qualifications.

November provides general Checkout support and a testing route without settling current defaults, eligibility or live rendering. Old raw lines 8-194 and new raw lines 9-166 otherwise show equivalent configuration behavior across formatting, Node-to-cURL examples and link changes. Preserve the correct exclusion key and wallet exception, the different deferred client and server fields, named method creation fields, and dynamic selection without an explicit method list, and both capture routes in source-stripe-payment-method-configurations.md with reciprocal Stripe index and configuration concept links.
